body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 22, 2026. Our top story today is the arrest of a 15-year-old suspect in connection with the deadly shooting at Independence High School’s football game last night. We’re also tracking a shooting reported at a Taco Bell in east Bakersfield overnight. It’s shaping up to be a hot one today, with temperatures expected to reach 100° and air quality at a moderate 74. Let’s get you caught up on the night and the day ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came just after midnight, when a witness reported seeing someone shot at a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area. Officers responded with an officer-safety broadcast, and the suspect was described as a white male in his 40s to 50s, wearing a black shirt and dark pants, sitting inside a white vehicle — possibly a Ford Explorer. Earlier in the night, around 2:16 a.m., flames were visible inside a vacant single-story house on King Street with heavy smoke showing. Multiple engines and a truck company responded, and the fire was under control by about 2:25. Just before 11 p.m., a two-vehicle collision left one vehicle on fire near Gosford Road and Harris Road. Engine 14 and Engine 9 responded — one car was smoking with another about a quarter mile back — and command dubbed it the Harris Incident. Injuries were unknown in that incident. Multiple reports of a grass fire drew a large response — engines, patrol units, a water tender, a dozer and a helicopter — to southbound Highway 395 north of Brown Road. Crews found a small roadside fire that was quickly extinguished, and the extra equipment was canceled. Around 10:38 p.m., an assault with a knife was reported with no injuries. The suspect — about 6 feet tall with neck tattoos, wearing black shorts, a gray shirt and white shoes — fled on foot northbound. Throughout the night, other calls included a subject reported with a firearm in his waistband on Houchin Road; an assault reported on Birch Avenue in Wasco; a hit-and-run on Monterey Street involving a black Camry and a white sedan; two fire hydrants reported spilling water on 22nd Street between Q and P streets; a small grass fire behind a residence on Windsong Street; a suspicious vehicle check on Culiacan Avenue; a family disturbance on Suncrest Drive involving an intoxicated teenager; a welfare check on a man lying on the ground near the curb on 26th Street; and an assault in progress with multiple people inside and a disturbance heard.

## Today's weather

We’re in for a hot one today, with temperatures expected to climb to a high near 100°. The overnight low will dip down to around 74°. Right now, it’s already 97° at Meadows Field (KBFL). There are no active weather alerts for Kern County at this time. Air quality is currently at an AQI of 74, which is considered moderate. No active fires are reported in the county this morning.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh has released a statement on the deadly shooting at Independence High School’s football game last night.** Mayor Goh expressed her condolences to the families affected by the violence and urged the community to come together in support of one another. She emphasized that the city is working closely with law enforcement to ensure public safety and that additional resources will be deployed to prevent future incidents. The mayor’s statement comes as the investigation into the shooting is ongoing, with police confirming the arrest of a 15-year-old suspect this morning.

**23ABC told us that Bakersfield Police have confirmed the arrest of a 15-year-old suspect in connection to the deadly shooting at Independence High School.** The arrest was made Saturday morning in the 7500 block of Stockdale Highway. Police have not announced any other arrests or identified additional suspects at this time, and the investigation is still underway. The shooting occurred during a football game between Independence High School and Centennial High School, prompting a heavy police presence on campus and a request for the community to avoid the area.

**KGET 17 said that with summer in full swing and many people heading to local rivers and lakes, it’s important to be aware of the warning signs of flesh-eating bacteria.** The bacteria, known as necrotizing fasciitis, can enter the body through even minor cuts or scrapes and cause rapid tissue damage. Symptoms to watch for include redness, swelling, and pain at the site of an injury, along with fever and chills. If you experience these symptoms after spending time in natural bodies of water, seek medical attention immediately. Health officials remind residents to always wear water shoes to protect against cuts and to clean any wounds thoroughly.

**23ABC announced that the Kern County Sheriff's Office has merged its emergency units to speed up water rescues in the county.** This consolidation aims to improve response times and enhance rescue operations in water-related emergencies. The move comes as deputies have recorded eight rescues and five recovered persons from the Lower and Upper Kern River since the day after Memorial Day. A recent two-day training session at Pyles Boys Camp near Lake Ming gave volunteers hands-on practice in critical search and rescue tactics, including techniques for grabbing victims from the water and bringing them up into the air. By combining water and aerial support, rescuers now have multiple vantage points to more precisely locate someone in danger, potentially saving lives more quickly.

## Something good

In a bit of positive news for our community, the Kern County Sheriff's Office has merged its emergency units to speed up water rescues in the county. This consolidation aims to improve response times and enhance rescue operations in water-related emergencies. The move comes as deputies have recorded eight rescues and five recovered persons from the Lower and Upper Kern River since the day after Memorial Day. A recent two-day training session at Pyles Boys Camp near Lake Ming gave volunteers hands-on practice in critical search and rescue tactics, including techniques for grabbing victims from the water and bringing them up into the air. By combining water and aerial support, rescuers now have multiple vantage points to more precisely locate someone in danger, potentially saving lives more quickly. This effort not only aims to save lives but also to teach the public what signs to watch for when someone may be in danger.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead to the rest of the week, there are several events and meetings on the calendar that you might want to mark down. On Tuesday, August 26, the Bakersfield City Council will hold a Special City Council Meeting at 12:00 p.m., followed by a City Council Meeting at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. If you’re looking for some entertainment, the Fox Theater has a full lineup of shows starting tonight with Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio. On Tuesday, August 26, you can catch the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027. Comedian Rodney Carrington will take the stage on Thursday, August 28, followed by CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on Friday, August 29. Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will also perform on Saturday, August 30. Be sure to check the Fox Theater’s website for tickets and more information on these upcoming shows.
